goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — Same silent-pass shape: asserts only `< Admin::AdminController`, never exercises show/update, so the no-op update endpoint is never caught.

adjudication.rationale: The spec at spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only asserts the controller inherits from Admin::AdminController and does not exercise the show/update actions. That is verifiable from the diff. However, this is a test-coverage weakness rather than a concrete defect introduced in the application logic. The claim that it "never catches" the no-op update endpoint is also not necessarily a bug: Admin::EmbeddingController#update intentionally just re-renders the serialized embedding, and actual changes (embeddable hosts) are persisted via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, not via embedding#update. So the finding doesn’t identify a clear correctness/security bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:19 — No spec anywhere covers `host_allowed?`/`record_for_host` even though it is the security boundary replacing `allows_embeddable_host?` (whose spec was deleted with the method).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds explicit test coverage for the new security boundary. `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` includes specs that call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` with allowed and disallowed URLs and with multiple hosts. This directly contradicts the claim that “no spec anywhere covers `host_allowed?`/`record_for_host`”. While `record_for_host` isn’t invoked by name, it is exercised indirectly via `host_allowed?`, which calls `record_for_host`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Validation regex allows an optional `:port`, but `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` which strips the port, so any host entered with a port can never match a referer.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbeddableHost` the validation regex permits storing hosts with an optional `:port` (e.g. `example.com:3000`). The `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and paths but does **not** strip a port, so a record can be saved with `host` = `example.com:3000`. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming referer/URL with `URI(...)` and compares against `uri.host`, which excludes the port (it would be `example.com`). The DB lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` therefore can never match a stored `example.com:3000`, making such entries ineffective for allowing embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Regex `[a-z]{2,5}` TLD limit rejects legitimate hosts (.museum, .software, localhost, IP addresses) that the old free-form site setting allowed; migrated rows survive but can never be re-saved.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new EmbeddableHost model adds `validates_format_of :host` with a regex that requires a dot and a TLD limited to 2–5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), and does not allow hosts like `localhost` or IP addresses. Previously, embeddable hosts were stored in the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` string and checked via URI parsing/comparison (no such TLD-length validation). The migration inserts old values directly into `embeddable_hosts` via SQL (bypassing validations), so existing rows can be present in the DB but later fail validation on update/save in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` (which calls `host.save`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — No uniqueness validation or unique index on host; duplicates are allowed and `.first` without ORDER BY picks a nondeterministic row, so embedded topics land in a random category.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` records used to choose the category for embedded topics (`TopicEmbed.import` sets `category: eh.try(:category_id)` after `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no `ORDER BY`, and the table/migration adds no UNIQUE index on `host` while the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of`. The admin controller `create` also allows inserting duplicates. Therefore duplicate rows for the same host are possible, and which row is returned by `.first` can vary, potentially selecting an unintended category. This is a real correctness problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — Broadening the hydration regex to `_ids` changes behavior for every model globally: any existing payload key ending in `_ids` is now deleted and replaced with a plural array that may be all `undefined`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Store._hydrateEmbedded` from matching only `*_id` keys to matching both `*_id` and `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the new `_ids` branch it *always* maps the id array through `_lookupSubType`, assigns the result to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then `delete obj[k]` (the original `*_ids` array). If the payload contains a `*_ids` field that is not accompanied by embedded records in `root` (or `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve those ids), the mapped array elements will be `undefined`/nullish, and the original ids are lost. This is a global behavior change affecting any model payload processed by this hydration step, not just embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:198 — In the `_ids` branch unresolved ids map to `undefined` and the original `_ids` key is deleted unconditionally, silently losing the data (`hydrated || []` is dead since map always returns an array).

adjudication.rationale: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-ids branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then always `delete obj[k]`. If `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id, the mapped entry becomes `undefined`, and because the original `*_ids` key is deleted unconditionally, the raw id list is lost (unlike the singular branch, which only deletes when `hydrated` is truthy). Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead because `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), so it won’t fall back to `[]` even when all entries are `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36 — After save the category is re-read from `Discourse.Category.findById`, which returns undefined for categories absent from the client store, leaving the row's badge blank despite a successful save.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:26 — edit` seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id`; when hydration failed to resolve the category this is undefined, and saving then sends a blank category_id which the server silently rewrites to uncategorized.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — Blank category_id is silently coerced to uncategorized instead of rejected, so a client-side ordering/hydration failure quietly reassigns an existing host's category.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:44 — destroyRecord()` has no `.catch`, so a failed delete silently leaves the row in place with an unhandled rejection and no user feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` handler. If the server delete fails (network/500/validation), the promise will reject with no local handling (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`), resulting in no user feedback and potentially an unhandled promise rejection while the row remains displayed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — update` is a no-op that re-renders the same data and returns success, so the controller's `saveChanges` action reports success while saving nothing.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb the `update` action does not read any params or persist anything; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, identical in effect to `show`. On the client side, admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` (via the new embedding adapter path). That request will return success and updated JSON even though nothing was saved/changed server-side, making the update endpoint effectively a no-op and potentially misleading/incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes an integer where the previous code passed a category name; if PostCreator/TopicCreator resolves `:category` by name the category is silently dropped to uncategorized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostCreator` initialization from `category: SiteSetting.embed_category` (a removed site setting that appears to have stored a category name) to `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (an integer). However, whether this is a bug depends entirely on how `PostCreator` interprets the `:category` argument (id vs name vs object), and that behavior is not shown in the diff. The rest of the diff consistently moves embedding configuration to use `category_id` (e.g., `EmbeddableHost` has `category_id`, admin UI saves `category_id`, serializer exposes `category_id`), which suggests passing an integer id is intended and likely supported. The finding’s claim that the category would be “silently dropped” is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore, so any three-word admin model type will never match ADMIN_MODELS.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath` was changed to compare `ADMIN_MODELS` against `type.replace('_', '-')`. While it’s true that `String#replace` without a global regex only replaces the first underscore, the only admin model types listed in `ADMIN_MODELS` after this change are `plugin`, `site-customization`, and `embeddable-host`, which correspond to names with at most one underscore (`site_customization`, `embeddable_host`) or none. There is no three-underscore/multi-underscore admin model in this diff that would fail to match, so the finding is a general theoretical concern rather than a verifiable problem introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13 — "raises an error with a missing host" no longer configures anything and now passes vacuously; the deleted "embeddable hosts not set" branch is untested.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example "raises an error with a missing host" previously forced the "no embeddable hosts configured" condition by setting SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil. After the change, that setup was removed, and the controller logic no longer has the explicit "embeddable hosts not set" branch; it now always gates on EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer). Because the test does not stub/set a referer (it just does `get :comments, embed_url: embed_url`), it will still fail access due to a missing/invalid referer regardless of whether any EmbeddableHost records exist, making the test effectively vacuous for the intended "missing host" scenario. Separately, there is no longer a test that specifically covers the "no allowed hosts exist" condition (empty EmbeddableHost table) distinct from the existing "no referer" test later in the file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic.rb:869 — expandable_first_post?` dropped the host-configured check entirely rather than checking `EmbeddableHost.exists?`, changing behavior on sites with no embeddable hosts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the “embedding is configured” guard entirely. Since the embedding configuration mechanism moved from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` to the `EmbeddableHost` table, an equivalent check would likely be `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. As written, the method can now return true on a site with `embed_truncate` enabled even when there are zero configured embeddable hosts, which is a behavior change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:65 — The `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` is now dead code since `record_for_host` swallows URI errors internally.

adjudication.rationale: The diff chunk for `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` only changes the host-check logic inside `ensure_embeddable` from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`. There is no `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` shown in this file in the provided diff, so the claim that such a rescue is “now dead code” is not verifiable from this change. The finding appears to reference code that is not present in the diff excerpt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:6 — saveChanges` is dead code — no template renders a Save Changes button — yet it targets the no-op update endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but the only new route template added in the diff (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) contains only the hosts table and an `addHost` button—there is no button or UI element wired to `saveChanges`. Additionally, the corresponding Rails `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is effectively a no-op (it just re-renders the serializer without applying any params). So, within this diff, `saveChanges` is unused and points at an endpoint that doesn't change anything.
